Name: Dhruvin Thakkar
Branch: IT
ID : 201080033
Year : 2023
Company: Dolat Capital
1. FIRST ROUND (Online test):
●There were 2 sections each of which had 2 coding questions.
●I obscurely remember one of those questions where we were given
an integer number ‘n’ as an input and we were asked to find the
union of all the prime numbers and fibonacci numbers (no repeating
elements) less than it.
2. SECOND ROUND (Technical round)
●It must have lasted for an hour and a half. As Dolat Capital uses C++ as
their primary language, the whole interview was based on C++.
●I was interviewed by 2 of their employees. To get started, they asked me to
introduce myself followed by the question ‘How much would you rate
yourself on the C++ programming language’ to which I answered a 7.
●There was an immediate follow up question ‘Why a 7 and not a 9?’. I
honestly reciprocated that I’m not good enough for a 9.
●None of the projects on my resume encompassed the use of C++ so they
asked me to give an explanation for it. I replied that most of the projects on
my resume existed because they were required to be made either for
academic purposes or for internship rounds😝.
●This was just a warm up as we can see that the technical questions have
not commenced yet. They started off with basic OOPs questions like what
does OOPs stand for, what are its four pillars, etc. They asked me to
explain compile time polymorphism, runtime polymorphism with examples
for each. I gave the example of function overloading for the former and
function overriding for the latter. I was also asked to write an example code
which explains function overriding on paper which evidently encompassed
the use of the ‘virtual’ keyword. Questions regarding constructors and
destructors followed by questions like ‘Explain inheritance, its types,
access specifiers, etc’ were asked which included questions pertaining to
the famous diamond problem(again the ‘virtual’ keyword). They also asked

questions regarding operator overloading like ‘What is operator
overloading?’ which also included writing an example code. Next I was
asked to explain the ‘static’ keyword.
●After checking on my grip on OOPs, they tested my knowledge regarding
other C++ concepts like pointers, strings, etc. I was supposed to give the
outputs for the codes they had written on paper regarding pointers and
references followed by inevitable questions on dynamic memory allocation.
Questions like ‘What is memory leak?’, ‘Explain the malloc keyword’, ‘What
is the difference between pointers and references?’, etc where asked.
Honestly, I wasn’t able to explain the ‘malloc’ keyword as it had been a
while since I studied it.
●Next, we moved on to DSA. I was asked to explain the difference between
binary trees and binary search trees. I was asked to write a code to merge
2 binary search trees on paper which I sadly failed to do. I was given two
numbers in the forms of strings and was asked to add them and return the
answer in the form of a string. Next, I was asked to write a code which
inserted a new node in a linked list at the specified position. Next, I was
asked to write a code which printed the following ‘*’ pattern:
●This is all I could remember from the technical interview. Of course I must
have missed on mentioning a few questions but all the major ones have
been cited above. At last, they asked me if I had any questions for them. I
asked them how it felt working here and how the working environment felt
to them to which they gave very positive answers.

3. HR Round
●Must have been 15 minutes long. The following questions were asked:
❖Tell me about yourself, your family, etc.
❖Why is C++ your primary language?
❖What are your plans for higher education?
❖Why did you choose this field if your father is in the field of finance?
❖Have you applied for any other companies other than Dolat Capital?
I think that's about it. That’s all I can remember from the HR round.
All the best!
